summary: Provision templated timebound partner workspace with automated channel archival and Confluence sync
description:
Issue summary: Platform team request to create a reusable project gateway that provisions a timeboxed 'partner-collab' Slack namespace, scaffolded Confluence space, and a light-weight Jira project template for short-term audit / partner engagements.

Business impact: Teams onboarding external partners currently create ad-hoc channels and spaces which creates long-lived guest access, inconsistent retention, and manual archive handoffs. This template should reduce manual steps, improve auditability, and ensure channels/spaces are auto-archived after a TTL while preserving an export snapshot for legal/audit.

Requested features: automated Slack workspace/channel scaffolder with RBAC snapshots; guest invite timebox (Okta linked); channel TTL with auto-archive and reason tag; Confluence mirror created at provisioning time with metadata page and exported channel transcript stored (attachments limited); permission snapshot (who had access) posted to Confluence space and retained for 365 days; Jira template for tracking turnover/closeout tasks; approval flow (manager + security) before provisioning for enterprise tier pods.

Who requested: Platform product manager (partner integrations) and Security.

Urgency: P2 — not blocking infra but high friction for partner rollout and audit readiness.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A — request/provisioning ticket rather than a bug. See acceptance criteria for gating requirements.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New 'Partner-Collab' provisioning button in the internal portal that creates a Slack namespace (scoped channels), Confluence space with a metadata landing page, and a Jira project from template.
2) Guest membership is time-boxed (default 30 days) and automatically removed at TTL; TTL configurable during provisioning.
3) Channel TTL auto-archives channel and posts an audit snapshot to the Confluence space (list of members, pinned messages, exported thread attachments).
4) RBAC snapshot stored as an immutable Confluence page (read: audit-only) and accessible to Security and Compliance.
5) Approval step recorded in Jira with approvers and timestamp; provisioning blocked until approvals complete.
6) All actions are logged to the central audit log and retain an immutable entry for 365 days.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-02: Reviewed Slack APIs for enterprise GRID features — channel export requires admin-level scopes and may be rate-limited for large channels. Confluence API can store HTML/PDF export blobs but we need to confirm retention policy with Legal.
2026-03-03: Security raised question on storing message content in Confluence (PII risk). Proposed approach: redact user emails and only store thread text + attachments metadata; full export gated to Legal/Security approval.
2026-03-04: Spike run to prototype automation using existing 'channel-provisioner' Lambda. Found two blockers: (1) channel export requires 'Discovery' scopes that are only granted to workspace admins with E-Discovery enabled; (2) Okta guest provisioning API exists but requires a dedicated integration client and consent from Identity team.
Prelim estimated effort: 5 engineer-days to wire approval flow + templating; 3 engineer-days for Slack export integration with rate-limit backoff + queuing; 2 engineer-days for Confluence export & immutable snapshot page.
comments: Maya Chen (reporter) — 2026-03-01: Opening this request after three partner rollouts where manual cleanup was missed. Example: Partner ACME project had 12 guest accounts remaining after project ended.

Jonas Patel (Security) — 2026-03-02: Security: need to confirm Legal signoff before storing message-level exports in Confluence. Can we instead store a hashed transcript + metadata and link to E-Discovery export behind access control?

Avery Kim (Platform Eng) — 2026-03-03: We can scaffold the Slack + Confluence resources via the provisioning API. Channel export requires discovery scopes. I'll open an integration request with Identity for the Okta client.
Action: Avery to prototype with small test channel and report rate limits.

SRE (Alex R.) — 2026-03-04: Note on rate limits: we should queue export jobs and use exponential backoff to avoid throttles. Also recommend retention TTL enforcement via a scheduled job so archive is robust to bot failures.

Maya Chen — 2026-03-05: Updated acceptance criteria to require immutable RBAC snapshot and 365-day accessibility. Please include GSuite/Okta guest mapping in the export so compliance can trace accounts.
proposed_next_steps:
1) Platform Eng to validate Slack export scopes with Workspace Admin and Identity (Okta). 2) Legal to confirm allowed export content and redaction rules. 3) Build approval workflow prototype in Jira with required approvers. 4) Deliver PoC automation for a single partner template (no exports) to validate provisioning flow, then iterate to add export + Confluence snapshot.
Owner: Platform Eng (Avery Kim). Target: prototype by 2026-03-20.
resolution: Draft plan accepted; implementation gated on Legal approval for message export. Provisioning automation without message export can be piloted for one partner while approvals are pending. Will convert to action tasks once spike confirms API scopes and Identity integration.
workaround: Manual checklist: Platform Ops can create a Slack channel, invite guests with expiry, and manually create a Confluence page with a CSV list of members. Documented in the partner runbook linked above.
notes: This ticket should be routed to Platform Eng and Security, and tracked from the Onboarding epic once approved. Retain visibility in #platform-ops and #security-review channels.
